astronix.title: Independent engineer - Astronix (formerly Altab)
paragraphs: Astronix started during my studies, under France's National Student-Entrepreneur Status: full-stack websites, platforms and e-commerce for my first clients. Today it's my full-time activity.

I work directly with my clients, including Airbus Defence and Space, on cyber engineering, full-stack development, tooling and automation, and process-improvement missions. I start from a need that is sometimes fuzzy and deliver a tool that runs, from design to deployment.
I bring a fresh DevSecOps perspective, security-by-design oriented, working with teams and their architects to avoid nasty surprises.

I started with vulnerability management for European ground segments (Egnos, Galileo, CO3D, PNEO…), bound by ESA's requirements. By rethinking the approach from scratch, I made the computations 1,400 times faster and 175% more accurate, ahead of ESA's requests. I quickly became the technical lead.

I then designed, on my own, a security audit solution covering an entire information system: software inventory, vulnerability management and prioritization, compliance analysis, obsolescence prevention, tracking over time, and reporting that became an internal reference.

Finally, I industrialized it into a full microservices web platform, adding an internal tool for software licenses with a validation workflow for specialists. I carried it end to end: architecture, development (Nuxt, AdonisJS, FastAPI, PostgreSQL), deployment across several segregated networks. Available from every European site, it serves thousands of users and saves several million euros a year.
Torn between continuing down the cybersecurity path of my degree and growing my freelance web-development business, I chose this internship to decide.

I led a team of three interns to design and build an app for organizing remote work, with a 3D view of the offices. From specification to delivery, using agile methods. This internship was the best professional experience I could have had, and it gave me confidence in my abilities: not only to learn, but above all to bring engineering, development and cybersecurity together.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Personal projects I design and build end to end.

aster.pitch: It's not just a CVE matcher, but an engine that composes attack chains. "An unauthenticated attacker reaches the front end, gets RCE there, pivots to the back end that talks to customer data." The whole chain, from scan to report, without installing anything on the scanned machines.
features: Agentless collection: CycloneDX 1.6 SBOMs and compliance findings, shipped as one bundle
Multi-source CVE matching (OSV, NVD, CVE List V5) with in-house version comparators
Path engine: eight kinds of steps, three attacker positions, minimal cut and bottlenecks
Dated results that also state what they don't know

yui.pitch: Yui runs around the clock and controls the apartment by voice or from its app: lights, TV, music, lock, shutters, timers, watering. The LLM only routes intents to tools, while keeping a context of learning, autonomy, proactivity and even humor. A simple command plays out in under half a second.
features: Voice pipeline: wake word, Whisper, XTTS
One MCP server per domain (Hue, Nuki, Spotify, Chromecast, Somfy, Gmail…)
LLM routing between a local model and the cloud depending on the request
Scenes, automations and proactivity (wake-up, leaving, coming home) with a mobile app

koya.pitch: Koya brings every configuration of my homelab into one place: from the nginx routes of the reverse proxy on a Pi to deploying a Node process on the deployment server, through monitoring of apps, services and even the router, with my own push-to-build/deploy system. A significant gain in time and lightness.
features: Deployment pipeline with history and per-step output
Nginx routes read and written from the UI

yoji.tagline: Notes, tasks and projects hub, + MCP
yoji.pitch: Yoji replaces Obsidian and Linear: I keep my notes, tasks and project tracking in a Git-versioned Markdown vault.
features: Git vault as the source of truth, database as a mere index
Sync with conflict handling and backups
Web, Linux (Electron, offline included) and Android

about: Passionate about science and a lifelong self-learner, I completed a cybersecurity engineering degree while running a web-development micro-business on the side.

Today I pair a DevSecOps mindset at work with active technical curiosity through maintaining my Homelab. This triptych (Code, Security, Hardware) gives me a holistic view of modern IT systems — and above all feeds my thirst to learn and build.
In short, a hybrid profile who can both quit Vim and center a div.

airbus.title: Cyber Engineer / Tech Lead - MCS Airbus Defence and Space
airbus.subtitle: On behalf of Neverhack
paragraphs: Through an innovative approach, I significantly optimized and improved many processes — x1400 in compute speed, +175% in accuracy, all while staying ahead of ESA's requirements. I quickly gained responsibility up to becoming technical lead, on fascinating projects such as building a vulnerability-management tool for European ground-segment systems (Egnos, Galileo, CO3D, PNEO...) to meet ESA's requirements.

I then designed a global security-audit solution covering an entire information system. The tool integrates vulnerability management and prioritization, obsolescence prevention and temporal analysis, ensuring a secure evolution of the system through reporting praised by Airbus.

Finally, I industrialized this solution into a full web platform (SaaS). Now accessible from every European site, it hosts many projects, makes daily work easier for thousands of Airbus employees and saves Airbus several million euros every year.
